newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cricket-England seek to restore credibility in NZ.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-England seek to restore credibility in NZ.

text.p: The England cricketers arrived in New Zealand on Monday determined to restore their credibility after an embarrassing one-day series whitewash in Zimbabwe.
"We are confident of beating New Zealand," a defiant England skipper Mike Atherton told Reuters in a telephone interview.

He vowed to take a positive attitude into the three test matches and five one-day internationals against New Zealand despite the soul-destroying losses in Zimbabwe. England drew their two test matches against the minnows of world cricket, and then plunged to a 3-0 loss in the one-day series.

"We performed poorly in the one-day internationals in Zimbabwe and we didn't do ourselves justice there, but I think the last three games blurred some of the good cricket we played in the test matches and we'll be looking to take that same positive attitude into the games in New Zealand," Atherton said.
New Zealand recently returned from a tour of Pakistan where they beat their hosts in the first test, only to lose the second and draw the series.

Atherton said his side had a healthy respect for the New Zealanders, but the return of paceman Dominic Cork, who missed the Zimbabwe leg of the tour for personal reasons, had bolstered England's hopes of victory.
"I think he'll beef up our side. He's a natural outswing bowler and we missed that in Zimbabwe," Atherton said.
The English batsmen failed to amass a one-day total of more than 179 in Zimbabwe and Atherton said they would need to re-think their approach to the shortened game.
But he rejected the suggestion that England lacked world-class batting talent.
"What we've got is six or seven top-class players all with test centuries. They've all got plenty of ability and I'm backing them 100 percent," he said.
Atherton's own tour has been dismal to date -- in Zimbabwe he scored just 34 runs in four test innings and 66 in the three one-dayers -- but he was confident of a return to form in New Zealand.
"Sure, my form has been poor in Zimbabwe. It's my challenge to put that right this time round," he said.
"We have a lot of respect for the New Zealand side, a lot of respect for what (captain) Lee Germon has done with them.
"But naturally, you've got to go into a cricket game with every confidence that you're going to be successful, and that's the attitude we'll be taking."
Atherton, who has been besieged by calls for his resignation since England's slump in Zimbabwe, also reaffirmed his commitment to captain England throughout the tour.
"I was appointed for the whole of the winter tour, which included Zimbabwe and New Zealand, and would not be doing my employers justice if I threw in the towel half-way round."
He said he would reassess his captaincy after the tour, which starts on Friday with a one-day match against a New Zealand Academy side in New Plymouth.
